a: CPU scheduling decides which ready process runs next on a core.
Round robin gives each process a time slice in cyclic order.
Priority scheduling runs higher-priority processes first (risk of starvation).
Multilevel queues separate process types (interactive vs batch) with different policies.
Context switches save/restore state and can be expensive if too frequent.
A page fault occurs when a needed page is not in physical memory.
Thrashing is excessive paging that collapses useful work.
COW shares pages until a write occurs, then copies — efficient forks.
User mode is restricted; kernel mode can access hardware and privileged instructions.
Interrupts signal the CPU to pause and run a handler for devices or timers.
